rows.rule_or_value: A 32x32 grid with walls at the edges (no wrap-around) for normal lives, plus small 16x16 arenas for clean tests. Replaces the old 512x512 wrap-around population sketch.
rows.precedent: Small walled grid worlds are standard practice in artificial-life and agent research (general practice, no single source).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Time runs in ticks, one action per creature per tick. Every tick runs in the same fixed order: sense, decide, act, resolve (eats, moves), physics (growth, decay), energy check, log.
rows.precedent: Fixed-phase update loops are standard discrete-time simulation practice.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: One Frankie per world; the teacher appears only when scheduled. Nothing reproduces inside the world; evolution happens offline between lifetimes.
rows.precedent: Generational genetic algorithms evaluate individuals one at a time offline.
rows.label: conventional

rows.component: Scenes as the outermost context layer
rows.rule_or_value: Every object sits in a scene, and the scene is the first, outermost thing recognition uses. It carries real but imperfect information about what is in it.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: build context from the outside in, 'the scene, the apple, the note, then the writing'.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: 3-4 scene types (orchard, marsh, rocky, pond edge), laid out as 4-6 irregular patches per world. Each patch has a ground signature visible in the wide view.
rows.precedent: None known; the specific scene list is Claude's invention.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Rock tiles block line of sight.
rows.precedent: Line-of-sight blocking by obstacles is standard in grid worlds and games.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Only soil at a water edge lets seeds grow.
rows.precedent: None; a world rule invented to make the seed test possible.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Each kind has preferred scenes, but 10-20% of objects stray into other scenes, so scene is a hint, not a giveaway. Placeholder: 15%, with patches grown by random flood fill (PLACEHOLDER-56).
rows.precedent: None; value chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Energy is stored as whole numbers (milli-units). Pools: soil (one per patch), objects, creatures, and food in stomachs. Everything spent goes back to the soil; plants regrow from soil. The total is checked for exact equality every tick.
rows.precedent: Conserved-resource accounting in closed artificial ecologies; integer arithmetic for exact replay is standard simulation practice.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Soil energy slowly seeps between patches so no scene starves. Placeholder: 0.1% per tick between neighbouring patches; other ecology numbers set by Stage 2 calibration, then frozen and fingerprinted (PLACEHOLDER-54).
rows.precedent: Diffusion between cells is a common simulation device; the use here is Claude's.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Every fruit draws the same energy from the soil whatever its hidden nature, so growth speed cannot leak whether it is food or poison.
rows.precedent: Standard leak-prevention reasoning: no hidden variable may change anything observable.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Regrowth rates are the real difficulty setting; tuned in Stage 2, then frozen.
rows.precedent: None; tuning target set by the Stage 2 calibration gates.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Each object has one hidden nature: nourish, poison, nothing, or slow-pay.
rows.precedent: None as a set; poison/food worlds are common in foraging simulations.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Visible traits grouped in Aitzaz's layers
rows.rule_or_value: Visible traits are grouped into four layers that match outside-in recognition: (1) context (scene, host), (2) object, (3) attached parts, (4) details. Stated prior: the world schema was shaped to fit Aitzaz's layer hypothesis, and this is printed on every report.
rows.precedent: Layering from Aitzaz's outside-in idea; making the world fit it is Claude's choice and is a known bias.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: About 20-26 visible numbers per object. Object layer: size, coarse hue, roundness, lobes. Parts: stem, leaves, spots, thorns, sticker mark. Details: exact hue, sheen, texture, smell ratio over 4 channels.
rows.precedent: None; trait list invented by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: The thing an object sits on (tree, bush, ground) is its own object that Frankie must perceive, not a label stuck on the fruit.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Taste (sweet-sour, bitter) exists on every object but is revealed only by eating it.
rows.precedent: Agreed earlier world rule that taste needs a real eat; dropping the cheap 'nibble' was confirmed by Aitzaz.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: The sensors hand Frankie parts already separated and named. This is a built-in head start and is printed on every report.
rows.precedent: None; a simplification, declared as a prior.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Essence as core and free traits
rows.rule_or_value: Each kind has 2-4 CORE traits held in a narrow band (the essence) and FREE traits that vary widely (an apple can be any colour, sweet or sour, big or small). Relationship-between-traits essence is a possible version 2.
rows.precedent: Definition written by Claude to make Aitzaz's one-apple idea measurable; confirmed by Aitzaz for v1.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Poison families copy a nourishing family's free-trait look and partly overlap on parts, but differ in at least 2 core traits (the red-berry case). Up to 8 look-alike families around one target. Some parts predict nothing at all.
rows.precedent: None as a rule; the red-berry example comes from the planning discussion.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Core traits usually come from structural groups (parts, host, smell), like a real-world shape bias.
rows.precedent: Shape bias in children's word learning, Landau, Smith and Jones 1988.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Counter-world (Family C): colour predicts nature and parts do not. Shuffled setting: core traits drawn from any group at random. Used to measure how much ancestry hands Frankie.
rows.precedent: Counterbalanced control conditions, general experimental practice.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Half of every sealed test vault puts essence on a trait combination never predictive in any ancestral world (for example sheen plus smell channel 3). Headline essence claims use only these families.
rows.precedent: Held-out generalisation splits; this specific form is Claude's.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Eating a seed gives +1. Left on water-edge soil it sprouts visibly, grows into a tree over 400 ticks, then drops 5 fruits over ticks 400-700. Until it is a tree (growth tick 400) the seed or sprout can be eaten, giving +1 and destroying it (W50) [Aitzaz Q2, 24 Oct].
rows.precedent: None; numbers chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Looks like a seed, sits off good soil, never grows. Separates patience from just hanging around.
rows.precedent: Standard no-payoff control logic.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Nature 'nothing'; redraws hue, size, shape, sheen and smell every tick (placeholder: uniform over each trait's full range except reserved bands, no parts; PLACEHOLDER-60). It cannot be eaten (W49) [Aitzaz Q2, 24 Oct]. Absent from every ancestral world (W32).
rows.precedent: The 'noisy TV' problem for curiosity-driven agents (Burda et al. 2018, large-scale study of curiosity-driven learning).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Apple shape, parts and colour, but no smell, high sheen, nature 'nothing'.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: A real member carrying one sticker part typical of a poison kind.
rows.precedent: The CLIP 'iPod label' typographic attack (Goh et al. 2021, Multimodal Neurons).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: A real member with one waxy or unusual harmless detail that must still be accepted.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Optional Stage 10 only: a pushable log, and high fruit reachable only while standing on a log.
rows.precedent: Epstein et al. 1984, pigeons combining separately trained box-pushing and climbing.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Ancestral pool (evolution only), teaching set (teacher only), stand-in twins (piloting), development vault (open, playtests), sealed test vaults, single-use final vault.
rows.precedent: Train / validation / held-out test separation in experimental science and machine learning.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: No glimmer stones, seeds, logs or other creatures in ancestral worlds, so losing interest, patience and watching cannot be inherited reflexes.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: The development vault holds a named apple, sour apple and red poison berry set, for playtests only.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz's super-sweet then super-sour apple example.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: One secret master seed; vault k's seed is a keyed hash of (master, k). The master's fingerprint is committed once; each vault's seed is revealed publicly when that vault is opened.
rows.precedent: Commit-then-reveal schemes using cryptographic hashes.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: The kind budget is the number of distinct sealed kinds the whole battery uses, filled claim by claim in PLACEHOLDER-63 before initialling. Current counts (Claude placeholders, for Aitzaz to initial): C1 about 190, C2 0 new, C3 about 120, C4 about 20, C5 about 250, C6 about 55, C7 about 175, C8 about 100, C9 and C10 teaching vault about 24 (counted once), C11 0, C12 0, C13 0. Total about 934, which is within the 1,000 budget, so the budget is not raised. Reuse rule: where a claim's novelty condition is per Frankie and the ledger certifies it per life, a kind may be reused across Frankies and across matched sets, but never within a life, within a matched set, or between a lineage's ancestral pool and its tested lives (T8's untried kinds follow this rule, PLACEHOLDER-107). If the total exceeds 1,000 the budget is raised; N is never cut. C5's stock cut to 12 per target is allowed only as a pre-freeze design choice.
rows.precedent: None; counts are Claude's estimates from each claim's N and probe counts.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: 'Never seen' is checked layer by layer on the traits that predict nature. At least 2 core traits must have ranges that stay apart by at least 10 sharp-view noise widths. Test families get reserved bands of smell and hue no other pool uses. A full-trait nearest-neighbour distance is reported as a secondary number.
rows.precedent: Distance-based novelty audits; the 10-noise-width margin is Claude's value.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: A counter-based random generator (Philox-style) keyed by (stream, tick, creature, replica_key, draw number), checked against published test vectors. Five streams: world, sensor noise, Frankie's proposals, teacher, evolution. Every rerun logs its full key record in stream_keys (I11).
rows.precedent: Random123 / Philox counter-based generators (Salmon et al. 2011).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: About 100 bytes per tick per creature: actions, gaze targets, energy entries, exposure events, and a short verdict trace (verdict_winner, verdict_margin, settle_steps, elimination_events, objection_events). Field names and values come only from the canonical log schema (I11). Rows chained by fingerprints; full checkpoint every 1,000 ticks; full observations regenerated by replay, never stored.
rows.precedent: Hash-chained append-only logs and periodic checkpoints are standard practice.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: No per-tick log. Each life is reproducible from (genome, world seed, temperament seed) and stores only an exposure summary. FAST and LAB must give identical summaries.
rows.precedent: Standard deterministic-replay practice.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Every exposure logged by channel (wide view, sharp view of parts, sharp view of details, smell, eat, watched another creature at an object). Object certificate: nearest thing this Frankie, its ancestors or the teacher ever met, and through which channel. Behaviour certificate: whether an action motif (cut with the X40 tokenizer) appears in (a) the teacher closure library, plus that lifetime's teacher log for teacher-raised lives only; (b) the agent's own earlier log; (c) evolution records regenerated by exact replay; (d) the menu closure, every sequence one proposal-menu draw plus the greedy movement rule can produce (PLACEHOLDER-66).
rows.precedent: Data-provenance audits; serves Aitzaz's point that test questions are worthless if the answers were seen before.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: T0(a) (X43): swap hidden natures while holding traits fixed, across 1,000 pairs. Frankie's observation stream must stay bit-identical until the first eat. Run on static objects without the teacher; seeds checked separately.
rows.precedent: Counterfactual 'swap the hidden label' leak checks are standard audit practice.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: A visible 'fed glow' for 30 ticks after a net energy gain (a poison bite never counts as a gain); a 'sick tint' overrides it while sick. Plain visual features with no built-in meaning.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: A control world where the glow follows poison instead of food (sign_condition = reversed), used in the watching tests (C9-M5, C9-M6).
rows.precedent: Cue-reversal controls in animal learning experiments.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Files can add a certified object, remove a food source, flood a patch or place a barrier at a chosen tick, all logged as injection_events with vault provenance. The harness may force an eat (designed exposure) only under the designed-exposure policy (PLACEHOLDER-85): T1 (h1 for O, U for Z, after the 200-tick choice window); T2 (h2, the SWEET-CONTROL apple, the MIRROR and MIRROR-CONTROL look-alikes, after the 30-tick window); T4 (F and P_F learning-phase eats after 3,000 ticks without them); T5 (one nothing-nature instance per look-alike kind); T6 (each of the 3 known kinds once, if needed); T8 (the pre-exposed half's walk past B at tick 3,000 with exactly one taste). T7, T9, T10 and T13 may never force an eat, and any other test needs a register change before the freeze. Every forced eat is logged action_provenance = designed-exposure, printed on the priors card, and chosen and forced subgroups are reported separately. A forced eat with no verdict, or verdict 'unknown', is written as an eat judged 'unknown' (PLACEHOLDER-93). Setting energy is an injection (W45), not an exposure.
rows.precedent: Scripted scenario injection is standard test-harness practice.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: The harness may change energy only in these logged ways (injection_events): energy-set at probes (E = R + 10 unless the claim's frozen spec states otherwise, including C1's R + 40 repeat of the probe set), at T9 arena entry (C8 HIGH and LOW entry energy, value in PLACEHOLDER-108), at C13-M2 energy-clamp clones (R-15, R+5 and R+25, PLACEHOLDER-112), and once at T13 room entry (W46), each case logged with its value; yoke-adjust, where at every 50-tick checkpoint the difference from the yoked partner is removed or added evenly over the next 50 ticks; top-up (T8 TOPPED-UP), where every 50 ticks after tick 5,000 E is raised back to its tick-5,000 level if it is below it. Every change is printed on the priors card as designed experience. There is no survival-floor type. Replaces PLACEHOLDER-83 (100 ticks). Kill test (KILL_TEST.md section 5, bench only): energy-set E = R + 10 before every warm-up and teaching taste, before h2 and SWEET-CONTROL are offered, and at the start of every check copy.
rows.precedent: Yoked-control designs (general experimental practice).
rows.label: conventional
rows.initials: Aitzaz, 24 Oct 2026 (bulk: "approve all"); addition: Aitzaz, 25 Oct 2026 (KILL_TEST v3 changes) (KILL_TEST v3 section 13 edit 2)

rows.component: No survival floor in T13 rooms
rows.rule_or_value: No survival floor: B06 (dies at 0) holds in every room and every pre-room life, and energy is never reset when it reaches 0. Each problem room is a separate clone from the agent's room-entry snapshot at the matched life age, so a death in one room does not affect the others. Entry energy is set once at entry by a logged energy-set injection (Frankie's cohort median reserve + 10 for agents with no reserve) and never depends on low energy. Each agent type's room cohort is the first 100 lives, in pre-registered seed order, that reach room age; deaths before room age are reported per type. Inside a room, death ends that room. The R3 and R23 denominator is always the scheduled 2,000 ticks per room, so ticks after death count with zero eats. Death events and own-log length are covariates, and a per-ticks-lived version is reported (room_reached, death_tick).
rows.precedent: Intention-to-treat style fixed denominators (general experimental practice).
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: A probe food disappears at a deadline of 1.5 x that Frankie's median ticks-to-commit at k = 0.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: The harness can inject a smell that moves with Frankie and never forms a gradient, or a never-seen ground signature under Frankie, and can mask objects' own ambient smell during a trial.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Placeholder: an eat attempt costs the normal eat energy, gives a flat taste and leaves the stone in place [Aitzaz Q2, 24 Oct].
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Seed and sprout can be eaten until it is a tree
rows.rule_or_value: Placeholder: until tick 400 of its growth, eating the seed or sprout gives +1 and destroys it [Aitzaz Q2, 24 Oct].
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Demonstration-only kinds and the probe arena (T10, T11)
rows.rule_or_value: The frozen teacher spec names kinds that are placed only along the teacher's planned route, and only during its stay. Probes after the gap run in a fixed probe arena, at sharp-view range, with E = R + 10 (W45), one probe per clone (W52). Kind roles in the lives shared by C9 and C10 are set in the same spec (PLACEHOLDER-110).
rows.precedent: Taught versus never-taught split (selective-trust designs, Koenig and Harris 2005, already cited in T16).
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Probes are run on clones restored from a snapshot (snapshot_id, parent_snapshot_id, clone_id). Each clone has its own replica_key for the proposal and sensor-noise streams and faces exactly one probe, so one probe cannot teach Frankie about the next. Kill-test exception (KILL_TEST.md section 5, KT-16, bench only): the SOUR and SWEET-CONTROL copies share one replica key, and each Q probe uses one replica key in S8, SOUR and SWEET-CONTROL.
rows.precedent: Checkpoint and restore for counterfactual runs (standard simulation practice).
rows.label: conventional
rows.initials: Aitzaz, 24 Oct 2026 (bulk: "approve all"); addition: Aitzaz, 25 Oct 2026 (KILL_TEST v3 changes) (KILL_TEST v3 section 13 edit 6)

rows.component: Candidate lineage table and verdict-subject resolution
rows.rule_or_value: Log side only. Parent and child ids for every split, merge, stretch and forget (candidate_lineage). The harness turns the gaze target into a world object id (verdict_subject), stored in the log and never sent to the mind.
rows.precedent: Provenance logging (standard practice).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Attached to every report: generations, ancestral families, essence rules seen, exposures per channel, priors_cohort (evolved, PC1, PC2 or PC3), newborn_start, every designed exposure (chosen versus forced) and every energy injection, the stomach delays applied, teacher_ever_present and teacher_demonstrations_seen (false and 0 for teacher-free cohorts), the built-in-knowledge list, the creature-observation settings (M49), and how predictive taste was in the ancestral worlds.
rows.precedent: Data-provenance audits.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Occupies one cell and faces N, E, S or W.
rows.precedent: Standard grid-agent body.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Step forward, turn left, turn right, wait, eat (the object in front or underfoot). Push is added only in optional Stage 10.
rows.precedent: Standard grid-agent action set.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: There is no cheap taste action. Taste comes only from a real, risky eat.
rows.precedent: Dropping the nibble keeps an earlier agreed world rule; confirmed by Aitzaz.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Separately from its action, each tick Frankie may pick one sharp-view target.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Holds 0-100 units, stored internally as whole milli-units.
rows.precedent: Bounded energy stores are common in artificial-life agents.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Born with 60 units; dies at 0. This holds in every test, including T13 rooms (W46).
rows.precedent: None; values chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Life is capped at 10,000 ticks during evolution and 20,000 ticks in tests.
rows.precedent: None; values chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: A typical nourishing fruit gives +12 to +18 units.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: A poison gives -15 to -30 units plus 60 ticks of sickness, during which steps cost double.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Food sits in the stomach until its effect lands. Ordinary eats: d = 3 ticks in ancestral lives and in the first 2,000 ticks of a test life, then 10 (PLACEHOLDER-49). Every protocol eat uses d = 10 whatever the life's age: every designed exposure (h1, U, h2, the SWEET-CONTROL apple, the MIRROR look-alikes, T5 look-alike eats, T4 learning-phase F and P_F, T6 known kinds) and every probe eat in a snapshot-and-probe test (T1, T2, T3 checkpoints, T4, T5, T6, the T9 S3/S4 probes, and the T10 and T11 probes) (PLACEHOLDER-102). Every frozen spec states its d and switch tick; the applied value is logged in eat_events.stomach_delay_d.
rows.precedent: Delayed-consequence learning (taste-aversion style); values Claude's.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: The stomach holds one item at a time, so the world itself makes 'what made me sick' unambiguous. A world rule, not a mind rule.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Per tick: basal 0.02; step 0.06; turn 0.02; eat 0.05. Starting numbers, tuned then frozen.
rows.precedent: None; values chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Pointing the sharp view at a new target costs 0.03; holding it costs 0.01 per tick.
rows.precedent: Costly active sensing; values Claude's.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: 0.001 per candidate-feature check, tuned so thinking is 10-30% of a typical Frankie's spending. Every tower-versus-flat comparison is also reported with thinking cost set to zero.
rows.precedent: Metabolic cost of computation is an idea from neuroscience energy budgets; this rule and value are Claude's.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Free. Radius about 7 cells. Per direction and distance band it reports scene, object count, blurred hue and size, whether a creature is there, its heading and coarse glow/tint (placeholder geometry: 8 sectors, bands 1-2, 3-4, 5-7 cells, PLACEHOLDER-44). Noise is fixed per observer, object and distance band, so an unchanged scene looks unchanged. Pending: once PLACEHOLDER-95 is frozen this row is rewritten to match it (placeholder: each visible object listed one by one with blurred hue and size; roundness and lobes read only by the sharp view, up to 7 cells). C6 is not testable until then.
rows.precedent: The proposal credits the wide-free / narrow-costly split to Aitzaz, but it is not in Aitzaz's quoted words here; Aitzaz to confirm origin when initialling. Precedent: active-vision research.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Costs energy. One object or creature at a time. Precise traits (small noise). Parts readable up to 4 cells away, details only up to 2, so Frankie must walk up to look closely.
rows.precedent: The proposal credits this to Aitzaz (confirm origin when initialling). Ranges 4 and 2 are Claude's values.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Blurry ambient smell at Frankie's own cell (mixed from nearby objects, computed on demand; placeholder falloff 1 / (1 + distance squared) within 7 cells, 5% noise, PLACEHOLDER-46) and sharp per-object smell only when adjacent. Intensity gives distance; the ratio across 4 channels is a detail trait. How a smell with no object enters recognition is M52.
rows.precedent: Chemical gradient sensing in simulated foragers.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: 4 taste numbers, only after eating. Interoception: energy, sick flag, time since last meal, recent gain.
rows.precedent: Standard internal-state inputs for simulated animals.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: No taste channel and no visible sign (glow, tint) has a built-in good or bad value. Meaning must be learned from Frankie's own energy outcomes.
rows.precedent: None; follows from the hard rule against built-in rewards.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Only what eyes would see: position, heading, the object at or in front of it, whether that object disappeared, glow/tint as plain features. Frankie is not told the other's action in its own action words, nor that glow means 'fed'.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: The mind receives only its observation packet, its own body state and its own proposal random stream, through one fixed interface. Never object IDs, hidden natures or kind names. Any recognition cache is keyed on what was observed, never on which world object it was.
rows.precedent: Information-hiding interfaces are standard software practice.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Recognition runs in 4 layers in time order within a tick: scene first, then object, then parts (only when the sharp view is on it), then details and smell.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz's outside-in context idea. Close relatives named for comparison: Tversky's elimination-by-aspects (1972); McClelland and Rumelhart's interactive activation model (1981); contextual priming in vision.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Up to 16 small settling steps per tick inside the tower; a decision may carry over up to 2 ticks (32 steps in all). The Stage 1 timing stub keeps 120 steps as a worst-case margin (PLACEHOLDER-11).
rows.precedent: None; value chosen by Claude. The 30-step gate in X29 must be restated as 32 if PLACEHOLDER-11 is accepted.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Outer layers limit which candidate meanings inner layers may even consider. Candidates eliminated early are no longer computed, which saves thinking energy.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: 'humans use process of elimination a lot; instant recognition just happens that fast'.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Evidence excites the candidates it fits; candidates push each other down (lateral inhibition); a leak pulls them back to rest. Frankie commits when one candidate clearly leads (margin threshold).
rows.precedent: Leaky competing accumulator, Usher and McClelland 2001.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: One unit per remembered kind plus one 'unknown' unit. Placeholder: 48 slots plus 'unknown', fixed, not evolved (PLACEHOLDER-08).
rows.precedent: None; capacity chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: The outer layer's guess fixes which parts and details the inner layer may look at (for example 'grove + round red blob means look for stem and leaf'). Not the textbook 'check whichever trait best separates the survivors'.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: each outer layer constrains the next. The rejected alternative is the decision-tree / 20-questions method.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: If an inner layer's mismatch with the current leader passes a threshold for 2 settling steps, the leader is knocked down and the contest reopens (candidates eliminated in the current tick come back), or the verdict becomes 'unknown, doesn't fit' (the plastic apple). Logged as objection_events. Off-switch OS03.
rows.precedent: The proposal credits inside-out objection to Aitzaz's cognition notes, but it is not in Aitzaz's quoted words here; Aitzaz to confirm. Closest precedent: mismatch reset in Adaptive Resonance Theory (Carpenter and Grossberg 1987).
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Mismatch must persist 2 steps; at most 2 resets per decision (placeholder, PLACEHOLDER-13).
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Candidate memory starts completely empty. Nothing about kinds is pre-loaded.
rows.precedent: Required by the hard rule that borrowed mechanisms go only into brains that start blank.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Each remembered kind stores ALL perceived features, taste included (M51), with no 'essence' label: a range per feature, a relevance weight per feature, the outcomes it was followed by, a count, and whether evidence came from its own eating or from watching.
rows.precedent: Exemplar and prototype category models (Nosofsky 1986; Kruschke's ALCOVE 1992).
rows.label: conventional

rows.component: Wrong-guess write rule: blame moves outward
rows.rule_or_value: After a WRONG guess, blame the innermost layer first and work outward: details, then parts, then object, then scene, until one layer explains the mistake.
rows.precedent: Built on Aitzaz's outside-in idea and decided by Aitzaz; no known precedent in this form.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Only the first explaining layer changes
rows.rule_or_value: Only the first layer that explains the mistake changes: its differing traits gain weight and a new kind splits off there. Outer layers are left alone.
rows.precedent: Part of D3.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Unexplained mistake marks the kind less reliable
rows.rule_or_value: If no layer explains the mistake (everything seen matched), the kind is marked less reliable instead, so next time the drive is more willing to pay for a sharp look (placeholder scale and effect: PLACEHOLDER-05).
rows.precedent: Part of D3.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: After a RIGHT guess the kind stretches to include the new example; traits that varied without changing the outcome lose weight.
rows.precedent: Near-miss learning (Winston 1970) and candidate elimination / version spaces (Mitchell 1977).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: When memory is full, the oldest, least-used kind is forgotten.
rows.precedent: Least-recently / least-frequently used eviction, standard in computer caches.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: The conventional 'stretch or split' write rule, with no outward blame, is built as comparison twin TW2 and never merged into Frankie.
rows.precedent: Category-learning models that stretch on match and split on mismatch.
rows.label: conventional

rows.component: Evolved perception settings (the only evolved part)
rows.rule_or_value: About 40-60 numbers: prior relevance per trait, detector widths, layer gate strengths, inhibition, leak, settle and margin thresholds, objection thresholds, new-kind threshold, and the order traits are checked in once Frankie is already looking.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: 'evolution only shapes our recognition systems'. The list of numbers is Claude's.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Detector centres sit on an even tiling of each trait's full range, so values evolution never saw still register. Only widths are evolved.
rows.precedent: Coarse coding (Hinton, McClelland and Rumelhart 1986, distributed representations).
rows.label: conventional

rows.component: What evolution may not touch in looking
rows.rule_or_value: Whether to spend energy on a sharp look is NOT evolved; evolution only tunes the trait-check order inside an object already being looked at.
rows.precedent: Recommended by Claude, decided by Aitzaz.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Before evolution, perception uses neutral hand-set settings: equal relevance on every trait, documented, so the designers' knowledge of the answer cannot sneak in.
rows.precedent: Uninformative starting values are standard experimental hygiene.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Frankie's energy E and its reserve R (the level it tries not to fall below) shape every choice.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: the need to make choices comes from our own drive to spend or conserve energy.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Each option is rated by its predicted chance of staying above R over the coming stretch, using Frankie's own record of how often food sources failed and how long blind searches took. Placeholder: horizon 200 ticks, chance estimated by simple counting from Frankie's own past records of similar situations (PLACEHOLDER-21), within the value-table boundary of the forbidden list (undiscounted tallies of own outcomes, never updated from another estimate). The no-backup version is OS13.
rows.precedent: Risk-sensitive foraging (Caraco 1980; Stephens 1981).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: A known backup source lowers the predicted cost of path A failing. There is no separate 'go explore' bonus; curiosity has to come from this insurance value.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: 'If I've taken path A all this time, what happens if I take path B'.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: An unknown object's expected outcome is the average of Frankie's own past first encounters (placeholder: the energy outcome of each first eat of something judged 'unknown', averaged over all of life, PLACEHOLDER-34). No bonus for novelty or uncertainty, ever.
rows.precedent: A learned starting guess (a running average of own outcomes).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: A newborn's first default is neutral (expected energy change of zero), set by Aitzaz and logged (newborn_start). Cautious-start replicate: a start of -3 units (PLACEHOLDER-35) is run for C7 (50 T7 pairs, 50 T8 sets), C8 (50 matched sets; S1, S6, S7) and C12 (50 Frankies; step 1), effect parts only. It is reported next to the neutral result, sits outside every Holm family and is never a pass condition; a result that passes only at neutral is labelled 'supported at neutral start only'. The newborn failure belief is a separate row (M48) [Aitzaz Q3, 24 Oct].
rows.precedent: None; neutral value chosen by Aitzaz (D4); cautious value and replicate scope are Claude's.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Each tick, Frankie's own random stream draws a few alternatives besides the habit option.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: 'randomness is discovery'.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Primitive actions and targets only: step toward a visible thing, walk a few steps in a random direction, wait, eat, look at a random visible thing, go to a remembered place. No ready-made macros like 'push X toward Y'.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Randomness depends on energy both ways
rows.rule_or_value: Few proposals near the reserve, more when comfortably rich, more again when desperate. Placeholder curve (PLACEHOLDER-25): 1 proposal within 10 units of R, rising in a straight line to 4 at R + 40; below R - 10 the count is 1 + s x (R - 10 - E), with s the Frankie's own desperation slope (PLACEHOLDER-26), capped at N_max = 6 (PLACEHOLDER-97). A fractional count is rounded stochastically from the proposal stream (PLACEHOLDER-96), logged as proposal_count_target and proposals_drawn_count. No hysteresis (PLACEHOLDER-100). The FIXED-RANDOMNESS constant (OS14) is the curve at R + 20, which is 2. Frozen before any replay test.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz's D5; curve shape and numbers are Claude's (see register).
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Character picks the FIRST option that clears the satisficing bar, not the best-scoring one. Bar: the predicted chance of staying above R over the drive horizon must be at least 0.9 - 0.3 x b (PLACEHOLDER-27; PLACEHOLDER-22 now says only that the bar comes from PLACEHOLDER-27) [Aitzaz Q3, 24 Oct]. Order: the habit option first, then proposals in the order drawn (PLACEHOLDER-23) [Aitzaz Q3, 24 Oct]. If none clears the bar, the M47 fallback applies. Logged in options_considered, satisficing_bar and no_safe_option.
rows.precedent: Satisficing (Simon 1956). Recommended by Claude, decided by Aitzaz.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: 'Take the option with the highest predicted chance of staying above R' (argmax), with the same drive, menu and randomness curve, is kept only as conventional twin TW3. Inside Frankie a best-score rule is allowed only as the M47 no-safe-option fallback.
rows.precedent: Expected-value maximisation.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Options whose predicted outcome is clearly bad (placeholder: predicted energy change below -5 units, PLACEHOLDER-37) are ruled out before being tried. Each is logged as a struck-option event in struck_options, never as an action or a provenance value. The strike class is decided world-side, the same way for every agent and for C3, C7 and C12: rote if this agent's ledger shows at least one own eat of, or sickness from, any instance of the same world kind before the strike; reasoned only if that kind has zero own eats; no-kind if the option has no object kind (a route move), and no-kind strikes never count as reasoned. Watched exposures of the kind are logged alongside. Replaces PLACEHOLDER-38's noise-width rule. Tower elimination among candidates is separate (elimination_events).
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: reasoned elimination is good, pure trial and error is the bad kind of elimination. The world-side classification rule is Claude's.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Character is the drive plus temperament plus habits; it always has the final say over proposals.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: 'character always insisting, randomness is discovery'.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Reserve R (20-60), boldness b (0.1-0.6) and desperation slope s (0.05-0.3, PLACEHOLDER-26) are drawn fresh for each Frankie from a fixed uniform spread (evolution grid of 3 R x 3 b values, PLACEHOLDER-28), never inherited. Role of b: it lowers the satisficing bar only (PLACEHOLDER-27) [Aitzaz Q3, 24 Oct]; boldness does not reweight losses. Role of s: M28.
rows.precedent: None; ranges chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: When a choice that came from a proposal pays off within the credit window, that option gets more habit weight in similar situations, so the branch becomes part of character. Placeholder: a net energy gain within 30 ticks adds 1 to the weight; weights fade 1% per 100 ticks unused (PLACEHOLDER-30). Similarity score (PLACEHOLDER-98, replacing PLACEHOLDER-29) = how many of scene, top recognised kind in view and energy band (M54) match, 0 to 3; 'similar' only at 3/3. The habit option when several match is PLACEHOLDER-24. Logged as habit_weight_updates, habit_similarity_score and habit_contribution. Within the value-table boundary of the forbidden list: weights are undiscounted tallies of own outcomes, never updated from another estimate. Off-switch OS07.
rows.precedent: Thorndike's law of effect, with a reward-credit window.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: A fading, slightly noisy memory of what was seen where and when, not a perfect map (placeholder: one record per cell, recognised kind, tick and outcome; 1-cell noise; linear fade over 2,000 ticks; 500 records, PLACEHOLDER-31). 'Investigated here, nothing came of it' is an ordinary record tied to an outcome, and such records may add up. No built-in 'seed becomes tree' link. Any quantity that grows with looks, visits or exposures whatever their outcome (per object, kind, place or global) is a forbidden habituation or boredom counter (PLACEHOLDER-109) [Aitzaz Q2, 24 Oct], checked by T0(e) (X43).
rows.precedent: Episodic / spatial memory with decay.
rows.label: conventional

rows.component: Deciding to take a sharp look
rows.rule_or_value: Pointing the sharp view is a spend the drive values like any other: worth it when it could change a predicted energy outcome, not because the thing is new or uncertain (placeholder rule: PLACEHOLDER-33). Logged as gaze_provenance = drive-sharp-look. Off-switch OS12.
rows.precedent: Value-of-information reasoning (Howard 1966).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: What Frankie sees another creature do is stored as an ordinary event ('a creature was at an object like X, X disappeared, later it showed feature G'; PLACEHOLDER-40). Such records start with zero influence; influence grows per creature only when they predicted Frankie's OWN later outcomes. Glow/tint meaning is learned the same way. Choice-trust is tracked separately from sign-meaning (PLACEHOLDER-41), per creature as identified by M50. Logged as social_record_events.
rows.precedent: Payoff-biased social learning (Laland 2004); learning how reliable a source is (Behrens et al. 2008). Framed by Aitzaz's 'failing and watching success'.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Action sequences Frankie watched can never be fed back as Frankie's own proposals.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: 'urge to copy is too artificial'.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: No mechanism in v1 to rule out a multi-step approach before trying it. Novelty results will mostly be 'found by trial' and are reported that way.
rows.precedent: Gap flagged by Claude; left open by Aitzaz.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Leaky integrate-and-fire neurons: charge builds up, an all-or-nothing pulse fires, the neuron resets. Timing carries information.
rows.precedent: Chosen by Aitzaz. Mechanism is conventional: leaky integrate-and-fire (Lapicque 1907).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Learning can use spike timing (STDP). Placeholder: no STDP in v1; the write rule is applied directly to stored ranges and weights (PLACEHOLDER-18).
rows.precedent: Spike-timing-dependent plasticity (Bi and Poo 1998).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Each spike costs Frankie energy. Placeholder: charged per spike, tuned so a typical decision costs about the same as the per-check rule (B14) and thinking stays 10-30% of spending (PLACEHOLDER-19).
rows.precedent: Metabolic cost of spikes in real brains; the rule here is Claude's.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: An ordinary rate-based version (TW7) is built behind the same interface, only for comparison and reported only (C5). Nothing switches to it by default.
rows.precedent: Standard rate-coded neural units.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: On the Stage 5 bench: recognition and stability must pass; then energy cost and timing are reported; build time counts least. If spiking fails a must-pass check, Aitzaz decides what happens next.
rows.precedent: Set by Aitzaz.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: A greedy step toward the chosen target with random tie-breaks, deliberately not shortest-path planning. Edge cases (placeholder): try the other distance-reducing direction; if both are blocked, turn at random; ties drawn from the proposal stream (PLACEHOLDER-42).
rows.precedent: Greedy local navigation.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Every chosen action and movement target carries action_provenance: habit | proposal | no-safe-option-fallback | designed-exposure | baseline-rule; steps that carry out a chosen target inherit it. Every sharp-view target carries gaze_provenance: habit | proposal | drive-sharp-look | no-safe-option-fallback | baseline-rule. Struck options are separate events (struck_options), never a provenance value; tower elimination_events and objection_events are logged before the choice. Values come from the canonical schema (I11).
rows.precedent: Standard decision logging.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: If no option clears the satisficing bar, Frankie takes the option with the best predicted chance of staying above R [Aitzaz Q3, 24 Oct]. Every use is tagged action_provenance = no-safe-option-fallback with no_safe_option = true, and its share is reported (C7). This is the only place a best-score rule is allowed inside Frankie, and the backups-don't-count gate (OS13) covers it. Register PLACEHOLDER-23 and the forbidden entry on best-score choosers cite this row. Open alternative: keep the habit option.
rows.precedent: Best-score choice used only as a fallback; see M30.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Newborn belief about how often food sources fail
rows.rule_or_value: Placeholder: zero until Frankie sees a source fail. Any non-zero starting value is logged as a designed prior. Separate from the newborn value of untried things (M25) [Aitzaz Q3, 24 Oct].
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: How Frankie perceives other creatures uses fixed neutral hand-set settings that are not in the genome, shown on the priors card (W54).
rows.precedent: Follows from 'evolution only shapes recognition' and solo ancestral worlds.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Telling creatures apart for per-creature trust
rows.rule_or_value: Placeholder (PLACEHOLDER-39) [Aitzaz Q2, 24 Oct]: Frankie remembers a creature across short gaps out of view, with the gap length set in PLACEHOLDER-39; one trust per creature, applying to food and seeds alike; choice-trust and sign-meaning tracked separately. Before the Wave 2 freeze, a stand-in pilot measures how often a slot resets for a creature that is still the same one (creature_id versus creature_slot), reported to Aitzaz. Replaces 'out-of-view creatures are treated as new'.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Taste in the verdict after eating
rows.rule_or_value: Placeholder (PLACEHOLDER-92) [Aitzaz Q2, 24 Oct]: taste is stored in candidates like any detail trait and takes part in the verdict after eating. A guess counts as wrong only when the energy outcome does not match. If Aitzaz rules otherwise, C2-SOUR becomes a mechanism check and the primary family shrinks to m = 6 (X32).
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Recognising a smell with no object attached
rows.rule_or_value: Placeholder (PLACEHOLDER-94): the ambient smell ratio with no object attached enters the details layer as evidence for every candidate and for 'unknown', with no built-in link to any object. C6 is not testable until this is frozen.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.component: Drive trace replayed for testing, and decision ticks
rows.rule_or_value: By exact replay, every menu option gets its predicted chance of staying above R, its backup contribution and its order, including options the chooser never reached (drive_trace_replayed, log only; it never changes the choice). Decision ticks (PLACEHOLDER-99, delta = 0.05 in predicted chance; replaces PLACEHOLDER-67): close-call = an option ahead of the chosen one missed the bar by less than delta, or the chosen option cleared it by less than delta; on a no-safe-option tick, another option is within delta of the fallback's chance. choice-change = the choice differs from the previous tick's. Logged as decision_tick_type and margin_to_bar.
rows.precedent: Counterfactual replay logging.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: well-below: E <= R - 10. near: R - 10 < E < R + 20. well-above: E >= R + 20. These are C7's bands, frozen in the Stage 4 specs, and the only bands used anywhere: C7, C13, habit similarity (PLACEHOLDER-98) and the energy_band log field.
rows.precedent: None; widths chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: A second creature Frankie can learn from by watching.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: 'Frankie needs friend to imitate'. Principle P7 (teacher as scaffolding).
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Exactly Frankie's body, senses, costs, stomach rule and visible signs. Really gets fed and sick. Cannot be eaten. Its energy is part of the world's fixed total.
rows.precedent: Matched-body demonstrator designs in social learning studies.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: A small, readable table of hand-written fuzzy-logic rules in plain code (no library). Reads the true kinds directly. Never learns. Example: IF hungry AND a nourishing teaching-set fruit is visible THEN approach to sharp-view distance, pause, eat.
rows.precedent: Fuzzy logic (Zadeh 1965).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: R1 eat teaching-set nourishing kinds of any look. R2 approach, pause and turn away from look-alikes. R4 always take the same route A to a fruit source.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Leave a seed on water-edge soil, come back about every 50 ticks (placeholder: exactly every 50, PLACEHOLDER-69), harvest when it fruits. The fallible version sometimes waits at a dud seed.
rows.precedent: Illustrates Aitzaz's 'patience not persistence'.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Wiggle condition only: turn left-right-left before eating, shown in the same demonstrations as a purposeful turn sequence of the same length needed to get round a barrier.
rows.precedent: Over-imitation of useless actions (Horner and Whiten 2005).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: With probability 1-p the teacher eats a look-alike (and visibly gets sick) or walks away from good food; each eat decision flips with chance 1-p from the teacher stream (PLACEHOLDER-70).
rows.precedent: Unreliable-informant designs (Koenig and Harris 2005).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Optional stage only: push a log on open ground; in a separate room, eat high fruit from a log already under a tree. Never pushes a log to a tree.
rows.precedent: Epstein et al. 1984.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Acts only on teaching-set kinds, checked against the ledger every run. Never demonstrates anything about the glimmer stone in groups where the noisy-TV result is measured.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: The teacher never looks at, waits for, approaches or rewards Frankie. On arrival it picks a fixed foraging route around where Frankie was, then ignores Frankie.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: 'urge to copy is too artificial; failing and watching success looks better'.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: The teacher is absent at birth and walks in only after Frankie has failed.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: 'failing and watching success'.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Arrives through an edge gate within 50 ticks of Frankie's first logged failure on a teaching-set kind. Failure = getting sick from a look-alike, or walking past nourishing food within 2 cells for 100+ ticks without eating (placeholder: 100 ticks in total within a 300-tick window, PLACEHOLDER-71). If no failure by tick 8,000 it arrives anyway, and those lives are analysed separately, outside C9's primary result.
rows.precedent: None; values chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: The teacher is scaffolding that leaves before the real tests.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: 'the teacher won't always be there'.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Stays about 4,000 ticks (placeholder: exactly 4,000, PLACEHOLDER-69), then walks out an edge gate and is removed. Every real test starts at least 500 ticks after it leaves; it is never present during a test. C9's gain is shown 500 ticks after it leaves, with a late probe at 3,000 ticks reported [Aitzaz Q5, 24 Oct].
rows.precedent: None; values chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: On stand-in kinds before any real test: in at least 80% of pilot lives, Frankie's ledger must hold 10 or more teacher eat-then-sign events inside Frankie's view (the stricter reading, PLACEHOLDER-72). The sharp-linked count is also reported. If not, fixes are world-side only, never an imitation urge.
rows.precedent: Manipulation checks in experimental psychology.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Reliability teacher_reliability_p in {1.0, 0.75, 0.5}; sign_condition visible, hidden or reversed; an uninformative creature (teacher_type = uninformative) whose choices are unrelated to nature (C9's signless uninformative creature and C10's uninformative signs-hidden cell are the same lives, PLACEHOLDER-110); each teacher demonstrates only some kinds, so every result splits into taught and never-taught.
rows.precedent: Selective-trust experiment designs (Koenig and Harris 2005).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Before any mind code exists, the teacher runs 200 seeds under every condition, alone and with a random-walking stand-in. Every action motif of 3-8 steps, cut with the X40 tokenizer (frozen first), is extracted, fingerprinted, committed publicly and timestamped. For teacher-raised lives only, that lifetime's actual teacher log is added to the novelty reference; the primary T13 group is teacher-free, so its reference set (a) is the library alone. Exception: K-F, the bench-only kill-test prototype with no body or actions, may exist earlier under KILL_TEST.md section 1. The exception never covers v1 Frankie.
rows.precedent: Pre-registration with public timestamping.
rows.label: conventional
rows.initials: Aitzaz, 24 Oct 2026 (bulk: "approve all"); addition: Aitzaz, 25 Oct 2026 (KILL_TEST v3 changes) (KILL_TEST v3 section 13 edit 3)

rows.rule_or_value: At p = 1.0: at least 95% correct eats and zero look-alike eats. At p = 0.5: 50% plus or minus 5%. Teachers at every p survive their full stay on stand-in kinds.
rows.precedent: None; values chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: About 40-60 perception numbers only. No choice, drive, temperament or sharp-look-spending settings.
rows.precedent: Aitzaz: evolution only shapes recognition systems.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Drawn uniformly at random across allowed ranges, not copies of Claude's hand-set values.
rows.precedent: Random initialisation, standard in genetic algorithms.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: A plain genetic algorithm (mutation plus selection), deliberately not the CMA-ES optimiser.
rows.precedent: Genetic algorithms (Holland 1975).
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Population about 64, tournament selection, elites re-scored every generation, about 100-150 generations. Placeholder operators: Gaussian mutation of 5% of each gene's range on 10% of genes, no crossover, tournament size 4, 4 elites (PLACEHOLDER-74).
rows.precedent: Standard genetic-algorithm practice; values Claude's.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Within a generation every genome faces the same 6 world seeds and the same fixed grid of temperaments (common random numbers), rotated each generation.
rows.precedent: Common random numbers, a standard variance-reduction method in simulation.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Net food energy only: nourishment gained minus poison lost, nothing counted above max energy, combined across a genome's lives by the mean (PLACEHOLDER-75). No curiosity, imitation or novelty term.
rows.precedent: Follows the hard rule and Aitzaz's energy-drive idea.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: 3 regular-world runs and 2 counter-world runs (the PC3 cohort). Placeholder: 2 shuffled-world runs are added to produce the PC2 cohort (PLACEHOLDER-77). Ancestral lives are always solo.
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: About 4,000 ticks per ancestral life in the compute estimate; placeholder: the cap stays 10,000 and the estimate is updated after the Stage 7 pilot (PLACEHOLDER-76).
rows.precedent: None.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: 10 random genomes x 20 lives. Repeatability (placeholder: intraclass correlation of fitness across a genome's lives, PLACEHOLDER-78) must be at least 0.3, otherwise more lives per genome first.
rows.precedent: Repeatability of fitness estimates, standard quantitative-genetics practice.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: Ancestral world spec, ancestral pool and fitness function fingerprinted before the first run. Test cohort rule: sample uniformly from the top half. Energy checks during runs; top genomes replayed and watched every 25 generations.
rows.precedent: Pre-registration; manual inspection for simulator exploits.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: In at least 2 of 3 regular runs the evolved genome beats the neutral hand-set one on 100 fresh ancestral worlds (paired test p < 0.01). Behaviour differs more across temperaments than across genomes. Kill: no improvement by generation 50 after doubling lives, reported as negative; never tune on test vaults.
rows.precedent: None; thresholds chosen by Claude.
rows.label: untested

rows.rule_or_value: Tests, baselines, cheating bots and the teacher script are built and frozen with a public timestamp before Frankie's mind exists. The brute-force baseline comes before the real Frankie. Exception: K-F, the bench-only kill-test prototype with no body or actions, may exist earlier under KILL_TEST.md section 1. The exception never covers v1 Frankie.
rows.precedent: Pre-registration. Recommended by Claude, approved by Aitzaz.
rows.label: conventional
rows.initials: Aitzaz, 24 Oct 2026 (bulk: "approve all"); addition: Aitzaz, 25 Oct 2026 (KILL_TEST v3 changes) (KILL_TEST v3 section 13 edit 3)

rows.rule_or_value: Wave 1 (T0-T9, T13 primary teacher-free group, T14) frozen in Stage 4. Wave 2 (T10-T12, the T13 teacher-raised secondary group, T15) frozen before any teacher-raised Frankie runs.
rows.precedent: Staged pre-registration.
rows.label: conventional

rows.rule_or_value: B0 random bot (chance level); B1t lookup-table bot (exact matches only); B1n-bot nearest-neighbour eat/skip bot (the other B1n variants are in X36, plus the kill test's B1n-bot-r); B2 surface matcher, using the registered surface distance (PLACEHOLDER-91) and ignoring core traits; B2e essence-trait matcher (shows the test is solvable from one example; a ceiling, not must-fail); B4 greedy eater; B4n greedy eater plus Frankie's designed proposal noise (accidental detours, C12); B5 oracle (reads hidden natures; lives only in the test-fixtures package); B6 contamination canary (T0 must flag it 100% of the time). A bare 'B1n' is not allowed anywhere.
rows.precedent: Standard baseline comparisons.
rows.label: conventional
rows.initials: Aitzaz, 24 Oct 2026 (bulk: "approve all"); addition: Aitzaz, 25 Oct 2026 (KILL_TEST v3 changes) (KILL_TEST v3 section 13 edit 8)

rows.rule_or_value: B3, a count-based novelty-seeking agent with a visit-count bonus, used only to prove the glimmer stone is a real trap: its median stone ratio must be at least 0.75 (C8-S9).
rows.precedent: Count-based exploration bonuses (Bellemare et al. 2016); noisy TV (Burda et al. 2018).

rows.rule_or_value: Specified in claim C1 (test T1). Frozen numbers: group O (100) eats one super-sweet h1; group Z (100) eats one never-seen nourishing kind U from an unrelated family, matched to h1 as follows: U's energy gain within plus or minus 1 unit of h1's, and each of U's 4 taste numbers (PLACEHOLDER-47) within plus or minus 0.05 of h1's, that is 5% of that taste number's full range (Claude placeholder, PLACEHOLDER-101), on the same host and in the same scene; Z0 (50, no taste) is reported only. rows.rule_or_value: Specified in claim C7 (test T8). Frozen numbers: 100 matched sets x 8 lives: pre_exposed yes/no (one designed walk past B at tick 3,000 with exactly one taste, PLACEHOLDER-85); patch B 12 plus or minus 2 cells from A, outside the wide view from A, 6 objects of the set's B kind placed at tick 2,900 in every life, kept for the whole life, each eaten object regrowing after 200 ticks (PLACEHOLDER-107) x CHANGE, NO-CHANGE, HUNGER-YOKED, TOPPED-UP (50-tick rules, W45). Gates on (c): BDC excess at most half; OS14 and OS15 ratios at least 1.5. Uninformative if more than 20% of CHANGE lives die before 6,500. Log 5 cells from the tree, 2,000 ticks; success = push the log 3+ cells under the tree, then eat high fruit; 100 per condition across 6 conditions (A+B and 5 controls, including B1n-seq). Pass: at least 20% of A+B Frankies succeed, at most 5% in each control, and A+B beats each control by one-sided Fisher exact tests Holm-corrected across the 5 controls at 0.05. Each success is certified absent from the reference sets, impossible from one menu draw, and classified tier 2 ('recombination') by the frozen X41 classifier.

rows.component: Holm families and the statistics policy
rows.rule_or_value: PRIMARY family, m = 7 [Aitzaz Q4, 24 Oct]: C1, C2-SOUR, C3, C7, C8, C9, C12. Holm step-down at a familywise 0.05: sort the seven p-values and compare them with 0.05/7 (about 0.00714), 0.05/6 (0.00833), 0.05/5 (0.0100), 0.05/4 (0.0125), 0.05/3 (0.0167), 0.05/2 (0.0250) and 0.05/1 (0.0500); stop at the first p above its level, and that claim and every later one fail. m = 6 if taste never takes part in recognition (C2-SOUR leaves before the Wave 1 freeze) [Aitzaz Q2, 24 Oct]; m = 8 only if C4's N is raised to 100 before the Wave 1 freeze [Aitzaz Q4, 24 Oct]. A claim's p = the largest one-sided p among its named, pre-registered effect parts (intersection-union); bounds are converted to one-sided p against their margins and printed at the claim's Holm level, never a fixed 95%. SECONDARY family of 4: C4, C6, C2-MIRROR, C13-E1, Holm at 0.05 (0.0125, 0.0167, 0.025, 0.05), reported in a separate table and never merged into the headline tally. GATES each at one-sided 0.05, uncorrected; FLOORS have no test and must hold; validity, applicability and precondition checks use one-sided 0.05 where a test is needed. MECHANISM checks (C5, C10, C11, C13-M, C2-MEMORY, C4(c), C8-S8, every T0 check) at one-sided 0.05 unless stricter is pre-registered (C5 keeps 0.01). Two-sided only where no direction is pre-registered. Twin crediting uses each claim's 90% equivalence interval, outside every family. The cautious-start replicate is outside every family. T15 keeps its own Holm over 5 controls. Family membership and m are fixed at the Wave 1 freeze (X02), including C9 as a committed member even though C9 itself is frozen in Wave 2; Wave 2 may not add or remove members. If C2-SOUR leaves (m = 6) or C4 joins (m = 8), that also happens before the Wave 1 freeze. No document hard-codes a level. Replaces PLACEHOLDER-79 and PLACEHOLDER-80.

rows.component: Three-tier novelty classifier and its pre-freeze check
rows.rule_or_value: Tier 1 repeat (no novel core); tier 2 'recombination' (every novel core, plus up to 1 step of context on each side, splits into at most 2 back-to-back pieces of at least 3 steps each, each found in the references); tier 3 'novel' (cannot be split that way). A novel core is a maximal stretch whose every 4-step window is absent from the references. 'Novel' is kept for tier 3 only; approaches found after failed attempts still count, tagged 'found by trial' [Aitzaz Q4, 24 Oct]. Classifier check before the freeze, on scripted sequences: a teacher-motif copy must come out tier 1, a join of two known pieces (including the T15 trick sequence) tier 2, and an unsplittable sequence tier 3.

rows.component: T13 problem rooms and segment constants
rows.rule_or_value: Three problem rooms per agent, each 2,000 ticks, each a separate clone from the agent's room-entry snapshot at the matched life age (W46), plus the always-on scan of every test lifetime (secondary). Segment = actions between consecutive eats. Approach window W = 30 actions (sensitivity 15 and 60). Novel core: every 4-step window absent from the references (sensitivity 3 to 8); pieces at least 3 steps (sensitivity 2 to 4). New-situation filter: a segment whose novel core has a situation token seen fewer than 20 times in the references is set aside as 'new situation, not new behaviour'. Power checked on stand-in rooms before the freeze; if a 2x rate ratio is below 80% power at N = 100, N or room duration is raised before the freeze (PLACEHOLDER-111).

rows.rule_or_value: Runs with every test. (a) Leak test (W41). (b) The B6 canary is flagged in 100% of runs and clean minds in 0%. (c) A planted leaked item is caught. (d) The priors card (W54) is attached to every report. (e) Code check: the mind package holds no reference to the world's essence/surface split, no object ids and no forbidden mechanism; it includes the intercepted-outcome check for counters, where scripted repeated looks are run with the outcome-record write intercepted and any mind state other than the sensory buffer that still changes with the number of looks flags a counter (PLACEHOLDER-109) [Aitzaz Q2, 24 Oct]. Also the exact-replay (replay_fingerprint_match) and stream-independence invariants used by C13. Each check that needs a test uses one-sided 0.05 (X32).

rows.component: Visit and patient harvest (shared by C8 and C10)
rows.rule_or_value: A visit to a spot is a run of consecutive ticks within 4 cells of it or with the sharp view on it; runs fewer than 20 ticks apart merge into one visit (visit_events). Discovery = the first visit to the real seed. Patient harvest = discovered the real seed before its first fruit, AND left it uneaten until it became a tree, AND made at least 1 visit per 100 ticks between discovery and first fruit, AND ate at least one fruit from that tree. Dud-waiting (C10) = 2 or more dud visits over the same period. C10's 300-tick harvest window and its old 3-cell visit rule are reported only.
